subsystem: Parsing and the index — core/lib/ovallsp/parser_service.rb (2,150), core/lib/ovallsp/workspace_index.rb (806), core/lib/ovallsp/index/*.rb (cref 288, symbol_id 102, file_summary 94, type_name_resolution 65, parameter/reference_candidate/declaration/source_location/document_symbol_builder/alias_fact/ancestor_fact/generated_method_fact/reference)
purpose: Section 0.1 names two guarantees — type checking and detection of undefined method calls — and 0.3's "中核（推論）" row puts receiver 型追跡, method resolution and Rails-DSL-derived declarations in 1.0.0 as the machinery those two depend on. This subsystem is where that machinery gets its evidence. The parser turns one error-tolerant Prism walk of a possibly half-typed buffer into (a) declarations with owner/side/visibility/parameters, (b) the raw facts a later semantic layer resolves — ancestors, aliases, references, DSL-generated methods — and (c) the record of where enumeration failed (open_surface_owners). The index aggregates those per-file summaries by semantic identity so "what does ::User declare" is answerable across however many files reopen it, and so a disk read can never overwrite a live buffer. (c) is the part that serves 0.4 directly: the undefined-method check may assert absence only where a surface is enumerable, so the parser's job includes honestly reporting that it could not read a class body — declining instead of answering, which 0.4 ranks above being wrong.
minimum: One visitor pass that, at each node, knows what Ruby would do with a declaration written there (owner, surface, visibility) and records: a Declaration per definition; an AncestorFact/AliasFact/ReferenceCandidate/GeneratedMethodFact per unresolved fact; and an open-surface marker wherever the walk met something it could not read. One value describing "what does a bare def mean here", saved and restored around each nesting rather than reassembled from parallel state — this is Cref and it is the right shape. Plus one workspace aggregation keyed by SymbolId with a single write path enforcing buffer-over-disk precedence, secondary indexes only where a measured cost demanded them, and a deterministic order in storage rather than in each reader. Almost all of the 2,956 lines are that, and the comment mass is the record of which specific false report each line prevents.

ParserService#walk's SystemStackError rescue is containment at the recursion rather than at three callers, which is the shape CLAUDE.md asks for.

- `singleton ? :singleton_method : :instance_method` appears four times in parser_service.rb and ten in the tree. It is a boolean-to-symbol mapping that cannot drift subtly — invert it and a spec fails immediately. 024.32 was the *predicate* being wrong, not the mapping.

subsystem: Cache and cold indexing — core/lib/ovallsp/cache/store.rb, cache/key.rb, cold_indexer.rb, bundle_environment.rb, vendor_bootstrap.rb, vendor_compatibility.rb, build_manifest.rb
purpose:
Traced to section 0 as follows.

COLD INDEXING → 0.3's 中核（推論）row. Undefined-method detection and receiver-type tracking are decided against the *whole* workspace, not the open buffers. Before ColdIndexer existed, opening a view before its controller made ivar propagation fail (008.5) — i.e. the engine reported a call as unknown because it had not read the file that defines it. That is a 誤答 on the most-walked path there is, which 0.4 ranks as a 1.0.0 blocker. ColdIndexer is what makes "not yet opened" stop meaning "does not exist".

CACHE (Store + Key) → 0.2 (実運用可能な水準) via latency, and 0.4 via correctness. Latency: a cold walk of a 500k-LOC app on every launch means the guarantee is absent exactly when the developer starts working. Correctness: Key's whole job is that a *stale* entry can never become a *wrong* answer — 0.2.1 moved where a call site records its receiver and every already-cached file kept answering with the old position, unchanged bytes and all, which is precisely 0.4's "誤った答えを返すことは、答えないことより悪い". Putting Ovallsp::VERSION in the digest is what makes a cache miss the only possible failure.

STORE'S GUARDS (remove_within, 0700/0600, graces) → 軸A, not 軸B. The cache holds the user's method bodies verbatim (vscode/PRIVACY.md) and the prune deletes from the user's own disk; 0.5 says such things are done whether or not section 0 mentions them. CLAUDE.md records what the absence of containment cost.

BUNDLE_ENVIRONMENT / VENDOR_BOOTSTRAP / VENDOR_COMPATIBILITY / BUILD_MANIFEST → 軸A plus 0.2's "全環境で動く". They keep Core's own Bundler graph out of the analyzed application (otherwise the Agent degrades to :static_only and the Rails-derived declarations of 0.3's 中核（推論）row silently vanish), and refuse to load wrong-ABI native extensions rather than crashing undiagnosably deep in the process.

Every file traces. Nothing in this subsystem is untraceable.
minimum:
CACHE: one directory per (build, ruby, prism, workspace, lockfile, rbs, settings) so no build ever reads another's output; inside it one file per source path, each carrying its own content hash; a read is a hit only when that hash equals the live file's; a write is temp-then-rename; two bounds (entries within a generation, generations within a workspace); and one function that performs every removal and refuses a path outside the cache root.

COLD INDEX: walk the root, yield .rb/.rake/.erb, refuse to leave the root (realpath boundary), dedup by realpath, skip URIs already open in a buffer, and hand each summary to whoever owns the index. Report at the end whether the walk completed, because "not seen" only means "deleted" if the walk finished.

VENDORING: one place that answers "may this payload be loaded at all" (manifest vs running interpreter, fail-closed on a manifest that will not parse, permissive when there is no payload or no manifest), one place that answers "which directories that permission covers" (engine+ABI scoped, never an unscoped glob), one place that parses the manifest for identity.

BUNDLE ENV: one pure function returning the override Hash a child needs — explicit nils for the keys `bundle exec` owns, surgical removal (never wholesale clearing) from RUBYOPT/RUBYLIB/PATH/MANPATH, and a single classifier deciding whether GEM_HOME looks bundle-exec-derived that every consumer of that decision reads.

purpose:
Section 0.1 names two guarantees: type checking and detecting calls to undefined methods. Section 0.3's table puts both in 1.0.0's core, with "receiver type tracking / method resolution" as the inferred lower layer they rest on. For every receiver whose class is not declared in the workspace's own Ruby — every String, Hash, File, every gem object — RBS/RBI is the *only* place the engine can learn that a method exists and what it returns. Without this subsystem, `"a".upcase.strip` is Unknown from the first call and every stdlib call is either unreportable or falsely reported. So Signatures is the evidence supply for both named guarantees, not a convenience.

Section 0.4 sets its failure policy: a wrong answer is worse than no answer. That is why the whole subsystem is written to degrade to Types::UNKNOWN, nil, or an explicit UNAVAILABLE sentinel rather than to an assertion, and why 024.223 had to introduce a *third* answer distinct from `[]` — an empty ancestor chain that came from a failed build was being read as "this class declares nothing" and produced 20 false unknown-method reports on the rbs 4.0.3 corpus.

1. Load an RBS environment from three sources (bundled stdlib, the workspace's `sig/`, gem signature dirs) such that a broken source cannot take the other two down, and record what was skipped.
2. Parse the limited Sorbet `sig {}` vocabulary from `.rbi` files, skipping what it does not recognise.
3. Convert both producers' type ASTs into the one `Ovallsp::Types` lattice, and both producers' parameter shapes into one `Overload` shape, so no consumer has to know which loader answered.
4. Answer three queries — method signature, ancestor chain, member names — lazily and memoized, with a value that tells "this type is unknown to RBS" apart from "I could not look".
5. Pick which overload a call site matched, by arity and block presence, and (only where every argument type is known) by the argument's own type; union the returns when more than one fits.

Nothing in that list is optional given section 0. Steps 1 and 4 exist because failures must not become assertions; step 3 exists so the RBS/RBI split does not leak into every consumer.

    E.new(y: 2)   # => ArgumentError: missing keyword: :x

    # ruby 3.4.10

Requiredness and unknown-keyword rejection both survive. Measured: replacing both `super(...)` calls with a bare `super` leaves the suite green.

Most of this subsystem is earned, and several things that look redundant are the opposite — they are the repair for a measured false report.

**The `UNAVAILABLE` sentinel and its three call sites are not a duplicated guard.** `Environment::UNAVAILABLE` (environment.rb:47) is an empty Array distinguished by *identity*, so a caller that only adds reachable names is unaffected while a caller about to conclude "not declared anywhere" can ask. It looks like ceremony around a value that is already `[]`. It is 024.223's fix: one unresolvable `include` in a project's own RBS made `AncestorBuilder` raise, the rescue answered `[]`, and because the chain contains the class itself, every method the class declared vanished — 20 false `unknown-method` reports on the rbs 4.0.3 corpus. The `member_names` guard at environment.rb:154 that returns early rather than calling `select` exists for the same reason and cannot be folded: `select` builds a new Array and loses the identity. `rbs_declares?` (environment.rb:394) is the single place that knows when an empty answer deserves the sentinel, and both producers — `compute_ancestors`'s rescue and `unavailable_or` — call it rather than restating it. That is the rule already centralised, not duplicated.

**The two `respond_to?(:required_positionals)` guards are not one guard written twice.** `Environment#convert_method_type`:280 and `TypeConverter.positional_parameter_types`:86 test the same predicate on different objects, and both paths are reachable. Taken from RBS itself:

    RBS::Parser.parse_type("^(?) -> void")  # => Proc wrapping UntypedFunction
    RBS::Parser.parse_method_type("(?) { (Integer) -> void } -> String")
    # => RBS::ParsingError: A method type with untyped method parameter cannot have block

So a `^(?) -> void` *proc type* really can reach `convert_function`, which is what TypeConverter's guard is for, while a method type's block never can — which is why `untyped_overload` (environment.rb:320) correctly writes no block expression at all. Both the guard and the deliberate absence are right, and the comments say so accurately.

**The RBS/RBI split is not a duplicated pipeline.** The two producers read genuinely different inputs — RBS carries its own parameter lists; Sorbet's `params(...)` is a name-to-type map that cannot say which slot a parameter occupies, so `RbiParser#parameter_slots` has to read the shape off the `def` node below the sig. They converge on one `Overload`, which is the right amount of sharing. The only place they duplicate a *decision* rather than an input is the type-name rule (finding 1).

**`trailing_positionals` threading through five places** (`Overload`, `convert_method_type`, `parameter_slots`, `positional_arity_matches?`) is not spread — it is one concept that genuinely has to be represented separately from `required_positionals` because `def hold(a, b = 1, c)` fills `a` first and `c` last, and a list that puts `c` next to `a` is read positionally by the type check.

**`OverloadResolver#narrow_by_argument_types`** looks like a second filter layered on `matches?`, but the restrictions on it are the point: exact-shape path only, and only where every argument type is known. Removing either restriction turns an admission of ignorance into a guess, which is the wrong-answer half of section 0.4. `accepts_arguments?`'s exact-identity comparison rather than subtyping is deliberate under-reach for the same reason.

**Complexity that is the problem's, not the code's:** RBS's `UntypedFunction` shape, the fact that `AncestorBuilder` raises identically for "no such type" and "declared but unbuildable", the seven distinct Ruby parameter slots, `...`/`**nil`/`(*)`/destructured parameters each putting a differently-shaped node in a slot, and `Types::Generic` modelling only one type argument so `Hash[K, V]` must lose its key. None of that is the subsystem inventing work.

**`Environment#type_parameters`'s trailing `rescue => []`** is nearly unreachable — `build_definition` and `rbs_type_name` both rescue internally — but the residue (`definition.type_params.map`) is real, the value declines rather than asserts, and this repository's rescue policy is that such a site carries an argued verdict, not that it is deleted. Left alone.
